gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a power station's "2× USB-C" can mean very different things for this setup. Starlink says the Mini needs a 100 W (20 V/5 A) USB-C PD supply. A Jackery retailer page lists the Explorer 1000 v2's ports as 1 × 100 W + 1 × 30 W, so only one port can run the Mini and the MacBook gets 30 W at most from USB-C. The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 lists a 140 W (28 V/5 A) USB-C port and a separate small USB-C1 that shares 20 W with USB-A.
standout_why: I compared against starsurf.com (best power station for Starlink Mini, 2026-11-01), which says only that the Mini needs a '100 W USB-C PD' port and does not discuss per-port versus total ratings. I compared against kilohour.com (2026-10-24), which lists ports as 'USB-C 100 W' or '140 W', says 'All 49 US models we track list a USB-C port rated 100 W or more', and never covers running a laptop and the Mini from USB-C at the same time or a 30 W second port. ChatGPT's own answers cite only the Starlink help pages for the 100 W PD need, and one of them recommended the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 without the 100 W + 30 W split. The Starlink help pages loaded empty (they need JavaScript), so I could not reread them. Our current page says the Jackery 1000 v2 has '2× 100 W', which this finding contradicts. No rival I read puts maker cycle-life claims on the same basis: Jackery's is to 70%, while Anker, BLUETTI and EcoFlow quote to 80%.
decides: Among the 1 kWh picks ChatGPT showed (Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, Anker C1000), the Jackery can run the Mini or a MacBook Pro from USB-C, not both at full power. The second laptop has to use the inverter or the 12 V car port with an adapter, and the inverter's idle draw lowers runtime (kilohour assumes 10 W for AC versus 2 W for DC). On listed ports, the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 is the better 1 kWh pick for an all-USB-C workday. Days per charge barely change: OutdoorGearLab measured 910 Wh usable from the Jackery's 1,070 Wh, about the same as the 85% derate ChatGPT used. The footnote on cycle life also favours Anker and BLUETTI: the same '4,000 cycles' is claimed to 80% by Anker and BLUETTI but to 70% by Jackery.
